questions.q: What is the actual goal of this capstone, according to the brief?
options: Proving you can design, build, and productionize a real orchestrated pipeline of your own, from a blank DAG file
Memorizing every operator name covered in the course
Copying an earlier lesson's example DAG exactly, unchanged
Passing a written multiple-choice exam only
questions.explain: The capstone proves independent application of the course's full toolkit to a real pipeline, not a repeated walkthrough.

questions.q: According to the brief, what must the Snowflake connection deliverable use, instead of a hardcoded credential in the DAG file?
options: A separate DAG with no relation to the capstone
A plaintext password typed directly into the PythonOperator
No connection at all — Snowflake access is optional
A configured Airflow Connection, used via a hook or provider operator
questions.explain: The brief requires a real Connection (Chapter 3's topic) used through a hook or provider operator, not a hardcoded credential.

questions.q: What must drive the sensor or branch deliverable, according to the brief?
options: Nothing — the sensor or branch can be entirely decorative
A random number generator
The current time of day only, with no other logic
Real data or state, not a hardcoded True condition
questions.explain: The brief specifically requires the branch or sensor's condition to be driven by real data or state, whichever of the two the student chooses.

questions.q: According to the brief, what does the retries and alerting deliverable require beyond just configuring the settings?
options: Removing the on_failure_callback once it's confirmed to exist
Disabling all retries so failures surface immediately
Nothing further — configuration alone is sufficient
Proof the alert actually fires on a real, deliberate failure — not just that retries and alerting are theoretically configured
questions.explain: Consistent with this course's 'prove it, don't just configure it' habit, the brief requires watching a deliberate failure actually trigger the alert.

questions.q: What order does this lesson recommend for building the capstone DAG?
options: Retries and alerting configured before any tasks exist
Extract and load working locally first, then the Snowflake connection, then the sensor or branch, then the dbt task, then retries and alerting last
The sensor or branch before the linear extract-and-load path even works
The dbt task first, before any data has been loaded anywhere
questions.explain: Building the linear path first, then layering conditional logic, then the dbt task, then proving retries/alerting last avoids stacking new failure points on top of an unproven pipeline.
